summary: When Yom Tov is on Friday, we may not cook on Yom Tov for Shabbos, unless we made an eruv tavshilin before Yom Tov.

chunks.he: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: When Yom Tov falls on Friday,
chunks.st: With regard to a Festival that occurs on Shabbat eve,

chunks.en: a person may not cook from the start
chunks.st: one may not cook on the Festival with the initial intent to cook

chunks.en: on Yom Tov for Shabbos.
chunks.st: for Shabbat.

chunks.en: But he may cook for Yom Tov,
chunks.st: However, he may cook on that day for the Festival itself,

chunks.en: and if some is left over,
chunks.st: and if he left over any food,

chunks.en: it is left over for Shabbos.
chunks.st: he left it over for Shabbat.
chunks.stMore: The early Sages also instituted an ordinance: The joining of cooked foods [eiruv tavshilin], which the mishna explains.

chunks.en: He may make a cooked dish before Yom Tov
chunks.explain: This is called an eruv tavshilin.
chunks.st: One may prepare a cooked dish designated for Shabbat on a Festival eve

chunks.en: and count on it to cook on Yom Tov for Shabbos.
chunks.st: and rely on it to cook on the Festival for Shabbat.
chunks.stMore: The tanna’im disagreed with regard to the details of this ordinance:

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: You need two cooked dishes.
chunks.st: For the purpose of the joining of cooked foods one must prepare two cooked dishes,

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: One dish is enough.
chunks.st: One dish is sufficient.

chunks.en: They agree that a fish with an egg on it
chunks.st: And they both agree with regard to a fish and the egg that is fried on it

chunks.en: counts as two dishes.
chunks.st: that these are considered two dishes for this purpose.

chunks.en: If he ate it, or it got lost,
chunks.st: If one ate the food prepared before the Festival as an eiruv and none of it remained for Shabbat, or if it was lost,

chunks.en: he may not count on it to start cooking for Shabbos.
chunks.st: he may not rely on it and cook with the initial intent to cook for Shabbat.

chunks.en: But if he left even a little bit of it,
chunks.st: If he left any part of the eiruv,

chunks.en: he may count on it for Shabbos.
chunks.st: he may rely on it to cook for Shabbat.

summary: When Yom Tov is on Sunday, when may people and keilim be dipped in a mikveh to become tahor for Yom Tov?

chunks.en: If Yom Tov falls right after Shabbos,
chunks.st: If a Festival occurs directly after Shabbat, i.e., on a Sunday,
chunks.stMore: and one wishes to behave in a proper manner and purify himself and his vessels in honor of the Festival,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: everything must be dipped in a mikveh before Shabbos.
chunks.st: One must immerse everything before Shabbat,

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: Keilim must be dipped before Shabbos,
chunks.st: Vessels must be immersed before Shabbat,

chunks.en: but a person may dip himself on Shabbos.
chunks.st: but a person may immerse himself even on Shabbat.

summary: How can tamei water be made tahor on Yom Tov? And which kinds of dipping in a mikveh are allowed on Yom Tov?

chunks.en: They agree that we may let tamei water touch the mikveh water
chunks.st: And Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel both agree that one may bring ritually impure water into contact with ritually pure water

chunks.en: in a stone vessel, to make it tahor.
chunks.explain: A stone vessel cannot become tamei.
chunks.st: in stone vessels on Shabbat in order to purify the water.
chunks.stMore: Impure water can be purified if it is placed into a vessel that does not contract ritual impurity, such as a stone vessel, and then lowered with the vessel into a ritual bath. The water becomes purified when it comes into contact with the water of the ritual bath. Although this is not considered proper immersion, water may nevertheless be purified in this manner.

chunks.en: But we may not dip it in a tamei vessel.
chunks.explain: That would make the vessel tahor too, which is not allowed.
chunks.st: However, one may not immerse the impure water in a ritually impure vessel in order to purify the vessel at the same time.

chunks.en: And we may dip keilim to use them for a holier purpose, or with a different group.
chunks.explain: The keilim are already tahor; this makes them ready for something more special.
chunks.st: Likewise, one may immerse on a Festival from one principle to another, and from one group to another, as will be explained in the Gemara.
chunks.basisNote: The meaning of the last phrase follows Bartenura.

summary: Which korbanos may be brought on Yom Tov, and may we lean our hands on them?

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: We may bring shelamim, but we may not lean our hands on them.
chunks.st: One may bring peace-offerings on a Festival, but one may not place his hands on them,
chunks.stMore: as this is considered using animals, which is prohibited on a Festival by rabbinic decree.

chunks.en: But we may not bring olos.
chunks.explain: On Yom Tov we may shecht only to make food for people.
chunks.st: However, one may not bring burnt-offerings,
chunks.stMore: apart from the obligatory daily and additional offerings of the day, because burnt-offerings are consumed entirely on the altar and not by people, and slaughter is permitted on a Festival only for the purpose of human consumption.

words.note: Burnt-offerings, which are burned completely on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: we may bring shelamim and olos, and lean our hands on them.
chunks.st: One may bring both peace-offerings and burnt-offerings, and one may even place his hands on them.

summary: May we heat water on Yom Tov to wash our feet? And may we make a fire to keep warm?

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: A person may not heat water for his feet,
chunks.st: A person may not heat water on a Festival in order to wash his feet

chunks.en: unless it is also good for drinking.
chunks.st: unless it is also fit for drinking,
chunks.stMore: as they hold that kindling a fire on a Festival is permitted only for the sake of preparing food, but not for washing.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel allow it.
chunks.st: But Beit Hillel permit one to kindle a fire on a Festival even for washing.

chunks.en: A person may make a fire and warm himself by it.
chunks.st: A person may kindle a large fire and warm himself at it.

summary: Rabban Gamliel was strict like Beis Shammai in three things. The Sages said his family was strict for themselves but not for everyone.

chunks.en: In three things Rabban Gamliel
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel was stringent about three things

chunks.en: is strict like Beis Shammai:
chunks.st: in accordance with the statement of Beit Shammai:

chunks.en: We may not wrap up hot food to keep it warm
chunks.st: One may not insulate hot food

chunks.en: on Yom Tov for Shabbos;
chunks.st: on a Festival for Shabbat ab initio, but rather one ought to do so on the eve of the Festival;

chunks.he: וְאֵין זוֹקְפִין אֶת הַמְּנוֹרָה בְיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: we may not stand up a menorah that fell on Yom Tov;
chunks.st: and one may not set up a metal candelabrum that fell on a Festival;

chunks.he: וְאֵין אוֹפִין פִּתִּין גְּרִיצִין אֶלָּא רְקִיקִין.
chunks.en: and we may not bake thick loaves, only thin ones.
chunks.st: and one may not bake thick loaves on a Festival but only thin ones,
chunks.stMore: due to the great effort entailed in preparing the former.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel said:
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel said:

chunks.en: In my father's house, they never
chunks.st: From the days of my father’s household

chunks.en: baked thick loaves on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: they would never bake thick loaves on a Festival,

chunks.en: only thin ones.
chunks.st: but only thin ones.

chunks.en: The Sages said to him:
chunks.st: The Sages said to him:

chunks.en: What can we do about your father's house?
chunks.st: What shall we do for your father’s household,

chunks.en: They were strict with themselves
chunks.st: who were stringent with themselves

chunks.en: but lenient for all of Klal Yisrael,
chunks.st: but lenient with all of the Jewish people,

chunks.en: letting them bake thick loaves and cakes baked on coals.
chunks.st: to allow them to bake thick loaves and cakes baked on coals.

summary: Rabban Gamliel was lenient in three things, but the Sages forbid them.

chunks.he: אַף הוּא אָמַר שְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים לְהָקֵל,
chunks.en: He also said three things to be lenient:
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel also said three things as leniencies,
chunks.stMore: in opposition to the view of most of the Sages:

chunks.en: We may sweep the dining room on Yom Tov,
chunks.explain: They used to lean on couches while eating.
chunks.st: One may sweep the room of the couches on a Festival, i.e., the dining room,
chunks.stMore: where they would recline on couches to eat, as there is no concern that by sweeping the room one might come to fill in the holes and level the ground.

chunks.en: we may put sweet-smelling spices on coals on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: And one may place incense consisting of fragrant herbs on burning coals in order to perfume one’s house on a Festival.

chunks.en: and we may make a whole roasted young goat on the night of Pesach.
chunks.st: And one may prepare a whole kid goat, meaning a kid goat roasted whole, with its entrails over its head, on the night of Passover,
chunks.stMore: as was the custom when they roasted the Paschal lamb in the Temple.

chunks.en: But the Sages forbid all three.
chunks.st: However, the Rabbis prohibit all three practices: It is prohibited to sweep lest one come to level the ground, it is prohibited to burn incense because it does not meet the criteria of permitted food preparation, and it is prohibited to eat a kid that was roasted whole on the night of Passover because it would appear as if he were eating consecrated food outside the Temple.

summary: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah allowed three things that the Sages forbid, about caring for animals and grinding pepper.

chunks.en: There are three things Rabbi Elazar
chunks.st: There are three things

chunks.en: ben Azaryah allows
chunks.st: that Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya permits

chunks.en: and the Sages forbid:
chunks.st: and the Rabbis prohibit:

chunks.en: His cow went out on Shabbos with a strap between its horns.
chunks.explain: The Sages say the strap is a load, not jewelry.
chunks.st: His cow would go out on Shabbat with a decorative strap between its horns.
chunks.stMore: Rabbi Elazar holds that such a strap is considered an ornament for the cow rather than a burden, whereas the Sages view it as a burden.

chunks.en: We may comb an animal with a fine comb on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: And one may comb [mekardin] an animal with a fine comb on a Festival
chunks.stMore: in order to remove ticks and dirt from its hair; the Rabbis prohibit this due to a concern that he might thereby come to wound or bruise the animal.

chunks.en: and we may grind pepper in its own mill.
chunks.st: And one may grind pepper needed on the Festival even in its own mill,
chunks.stMore: although this appears similar to a weekday labor.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: אֵין מְקָרְדִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: We may not comb an animal with a fine comb on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: One may not comb an animal to remove ticks and dirt from its hair on a Festival

chunks.en: because it makes a sore.
chunks.st: because this certainly creates a wound,

chunks.en: But we may brush it with a soft comb.
chunks.st: but one may brush it with a wooden comb, as its blunt teeth do not wound the animal.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: But the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: We may not comb, and not even brush.
chunks.st: One may not comb, nor may one even brush.

summary: A pepper mill is made of three parts, and each part can become tamei on its own.

chunks.en: A pepper mill can become tamei
chunks.st: The aforementioned pepper mill
chunks.stMore: is a composite vessel, and each of its parts must be considered independently with respect to ritual impurity.

chunks.en: because it is three keilim:
chunks.st: It is susceptible to ritual impurity because of each of the three vessels of which it is comprised:

chunks.en: because it is a vessel that holds things,
chunks.st: It is susceptible to impurity because it is a wooden receptacle,

chunks.en: because it is a metal vessel,
chunks.st: it is susceptible to impurity because it is a metal vessel,

chunks.en: and because it is a sifter.
chunks.st: and it is susceptible to impurity because it is a sieve.

summary: A child's wagon can become tamei. May we pull it along the ground on Shabbos?

chunks.en: A child's toy wagon can become tamei from being sat on,
chunks.st: A child’s wagon, with which he plays and upon which he also sits, is susceptible to ritual impurity imparted by treading.
chunks.stMore: It is considered a fixed seat of the child, so that if the child is a zav and he sits on the wagon, it contracts the ritual impurity imparted by the treading of a zav.

words.note: Midras: a kind of tumah that comes from sitting or leaning on a thing.

chunks.en: and it may be moved on Shabbos.
chunks.st: And this wagon may be handled on Shabbat, as it is considered a vessel.

chunks.he: וְאֵינָהּ נִגְרֶרֶת אֶלָּא עַל גַּבֵּי כֵלִים.
chunks.en: But it may be pulled only over cloths.
chunks.explain: Otherwise it would make a groove in the ground, like plowing.
chunks.st: And it may be dragged on the ground on Shabbat only upon cloth,
chunks.stMore: a stone pavement, or the like, as otherwise it would create a furrow when dragged, and one would be liable due to the prohibited labor of plowing.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: No keilim may be pulled on the ground
chunks.st: For this reason, no vessels may be dragged on the ground on Shabbat

chunks.en: except a wagon,
chunks.st: except for a wagon,

chunks.en: because it only presses the earth down.
chunks.st: which is permitted because its wheels do not make a furrow in the ground but merely press the earth down. Since no earth is moved from its place, this is not considered digging or plowing on Shabbat.
